title: Money in whole cents
description:
Floating point cannot hold 0.10 exactly, so money is safer as whole cents. Write:

```python
def to_cents(text)          # "12.34" -> 1234, "5" -> 500, "0.5" -> 50, "7.05" -> 705 (at most two decimals, no sign)
def show(cents)             # 1234 -> "12.34", 5 -> "0.05", 100 -> "1.00"
def close_enough(a, b)      # True when two floats differ by less than one billionth
```

Read the text yourself, without `float()`: split it at the point with `text.split(".")`. You may use `int()` for the parts. `n // 100` and `n % 100` give the whole amount and the cents; an f-string with `:02d` pads a number to two digits (`f"{5:02d}"` is `"05"`).
hints: `parts = text.split(".")` gives the whole part and, if there was a point, the fraction. Pad the fraction to two digits (`"5"` means 50 cents) with `(parts[1] + "00")[:2]`.
For `show`, `cents // 100` is the whole amount and `cents % 100` the cents; `f"{x:02d}"` writes 5 as `05`.
rules: Read the amount without `float()`: that is the whole point.
